findings: F1 (fix-mechanism, confirmed): Parent unit sets CapabilityBoundingSet= (empty) and AmbientCapabilities= (empty). With an empty bounding set, root does NOT hold CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, so permission checks on the 0600 ledger file owned by uid 63764 fail with EACCES - the stated root cause is correct systemd/kernel behaviour, not a guess. The v3 drop-in assigns CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH. Plain (non-+/-) assignment to this directive REPLACES the empty set; it does not append. For User=root, effective capabilities are taken from the bounding set, so the granted caps take effect without any AmbientCapabilities change. Root + CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE can read a 0600 file regardless of owner: the EACCES is fixed.

F2 (security, sound): CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE does grant write-side DAC bypass on any file the process can reach. The effective guard is ProtectSystem=strict, which mounts the whole hierarchy read-only except ReadWritePaths=/var/backups/enhanced-cognee; capability bits cannot override EROFS (a read-only mount fails writes at the VFS layer before DAC matters). Writes remain possible only inside /var/backups/enhanced-cognee, which the parent unit already granted. No new writable path, no privilege escalation path: NoNewPrivileges=yes, RestrictSUIDSGID=yes, PrivateTmp/PrivateDevices/ProtectHome all retained and unmodified.

F3 (residual risk, fail-closed confirmed): The ledger step targets /var/lib/... on the read-only mount. Any write attempt - including sqlite attempting to open the db read-write or create a -journal/-wal file in that directory - fails at open() with EROFS. EROFS is a hard error, not a fallback, so the step cannot silently corrupt or partially mutate the ledger. Output goes only to /var/backups/enhanced-cognee (writable). If ledger_tools ever uses sqlite temp storage, PrivateTmp confines it to a private tmpfs, away from the ledger.

F4 (minimal-grant observation, non-blocking): Reading a 0600 file needs only CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH; CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE (write-side) is strictly broader than necessary for this fix. Given F2's read-only guard the exposure is nil-to-negligible, so this is a hardening option (drop CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, keep only CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH), not a defect.

F5 (drift risk, non-blocking): The drop-in uses ExecStart= (empty reset) then re-declares BOTH steps, including the parent's original database-backup step verbatim. This is correct drop-in technique (ExecStart is a list; a bare addition would append a third step), but it means the drop-in fully owns the ExecStart list. If the parent unit's first step is ever changed, this drop-in silently overrides it and the change will not take effect. Recommend a comment or check in future package updates; current content matches the parent exactly (verified against /etc/systemd/system/enhanced-cognee-backup.service).

F6 (drop-in scope, clean): The file contains exactly two directives - CapabilityBoundingSet (one line) and the ExecStart reset/re-add block. No other setting (ReadWritePaths, ProtectSystem, NoNewPrivileges, UMask, resource limits, credentials) is re-set, so nothing else is accidentally reset or weakened.
